Use Avogadro from Java, Kotlin, Scala, or scripts

Update molecules, read their data, and prepare previews contains complete examples for updating data and closing the resources your code creates.

Choose Java, Kotlin, Scala, Groovy, or ZenScript to build water, register it for a bucket, and query the result. Later examples draw the model and export a GIF. Each language calls the same Java implementation and follows the same registration and cleanup rules.

Calls used in the examples

Calls used in this guide
Call or setting Arguments What it does
AvogadroApi.builder(id) Namespaced molecule ID Create a definition using the same validation rules in every language.
owner(name).register(definition) Owner name; model definition Publish a definition and handle its asynchronous outcome.
owner(name).replace(batch) Owner name; complete replacement batch Replace the set controlled by that owner.
getOption / getOrNull Molecule identifier Use the native-language lookup helper when a missing result is expected.

When you finish: A builder creates a model but does not add it to the game. Java registrations use a name, called an owner, to group the definitions your mod controls; choose your mod ID. A RegistrationJob lets you cancel pending work or remove its installed set later. JSON and Groovy registrations use their file or script loading rules instead. Keep drawing and exports in client code. Scala futures observe existing jobs; retain the RegistrationJob itself when you need cancellation or release.

Install the support needed by your language

Java integrations need no language helper. Kotlin users need a compatible Kotlin runtime, and Scala helpers need Scalar for Scala 3; Scalar Legacy supplies Scala 2.11. For Groovy, install GroovyScript and put registrations in its reloadable postInit scripts. CraftTweaker scripts load at startup and need a restart after edits. All examples use the same rules for checking atoms, bonds, and item/fluid matches; choosing a language does not change those rules.

The common authoring APIs are safe outside the client. Rendering, GUI and media helpers belong in client-only classes or client events. Every geometry below is authored explicitly or through the supported SMILES interpreter; formulas alone do not determine connectivity. The library does not register these examples automatically.

Look up definitions and watch registration

Scala users can import Avogadro.* for getOption, definitionsVector and a registration job's completionFuture. The vector is an immutable copy in molecule-ID order, containing the original shared definitions. Retaining it does not follow later reloads. Kotlin's Avogadro.getOrNull extension makes missing results explicitly nullable. 

import io.github.wurtzitane.avogadro.scala.Avogadro.*
// Before: Avogadro.register(owner, water).whenComplete(...)
// After: a normal Scala Future, using your own ExecutionContext for callbacks.
val published = registerFuture("my_mod", water)
// Also available: replaceFuture(owner)(batch => ...) and moleculeFuture(id)(builder => ...).

These methods submit through the existing Java engine. Builder blocks run immediately; builder errors can throw before a future is returned. Asynchronous failures fail the returned future. No helper blocks a game thread or selects a game executor. Scala futures observe completion; retain the shared RegistrationJob when cancellation or release is needed.

Optional Kotlin coroutines

The ordinary Kotlin facade needs only the Kotlin runtime. The separate AvogadroCoroutines object requires kotlinx-coroutines-core (compiled against 1.7.3); it is not bundled. Only code using these helpers needs that dependency. Use registerAwait, replaceAwait, moleculeAwait, or import its awaitCompletion extension for an existing job's completion stage. 

import io.github.wurtzitane.avogadro.kotlin.AvogadroCoroutines
// Inside your existing coroutine; do not use runBlocking in a game callback.
val view = AvogadroCoroutines.registerAwait("my_mod", water)

Cancelling the coroutine stops waiting for the result; the molecule calculation or registration continues. It does not undo registered changes or remove the set installed by your mod. Keep a job and call its cancellation or release methods explicitly when needed. The operation may finish on another thread, while your coroutine context controls where execution resumes. Schedule Minecraft UI work on the client thread. Groovy still uses closures and ordinary collections; CraftTweaker uses its typed callbacks and job objects.

Register water and show it for a bucket

This registers water and makes it appear for a water bucket and the water fluid. The string my_mod identifies the mod’s registration set. Supplying an actual item or fluid stack also lets matching check its metadata and NBT tags. 

import io.github.wurtzitane.avogadro.api.*;

public class WaterRegistration {
    public static void registerWater() {
        var water = AvogadroApi.builder("my_mod:water")
            .name("Water").smiles("[H]O[H]")
            .items("minecraft:water_bucket").fluids("water").build();
        AvogadroApi.owner("my_mod").register(water)
            .whenComplete((view, error) -> { if (error != null) error.printStackTrace(); });
    }
}


import io.github.wurtzitane.avogadro.kotlin.Avogadro

fun registerWater() {
    val water = Avogadro.molecule("my_mod:water") {
        name("Water"); smiles("[H]O[H]")
        items("minecraft:water_bucket"); fluids("water")
    }
    Avogadro.register("my_mod", water).whenComplete { view, error ->
        if (error != null) error.printStackTrace()
    }
}


// groovy/postInit/molecules.groovy
def molecules = mods.avogadro.molecules
molecules.register('my_pack:water') {
    name('Water'); smiles('[H]O[H]')
    items('minecraft:water_bucket'); fluids('water')
}

import io.github.wurtzitane.avogadro.scala.Avogadro

object WaterRegistration {
  def registerWater(): Unit = {
    val water = Avogadro.molecule("my_mod:water") { m =>
      m.name("Water").smiles("[H]O[H]").items("minecraft:water_bucket").fluids("water")
    }
    Avogadro.register("my_mod", water).whenComplete { (view, error) =>
      if error != null then error.printStackTrace()
    }
  }
}


import mods.avogadro.Molecules;
Molecules.molecule("my_pack:water").name("Water").smiles("[H]O[H]")
    .itemSelector("minecraft:water_bucket").fluidSelector("minecraft:water").register();

The returned future completes when the definitions have passed validation and become available. Handle failure in a completion callback; do not block a game thread with join(). CraftTweaker records a copy of the submitted data in a logged startup action. Groovy checks the complete script registration set before applying it, keeping the previous set if validation fails.

Replace all molecules registered by your mod

Use replacement when reloading your mod’s complete molecule list. The example keeps water and removes any earlier entries omitted from the replacement for that same registration identifier. Other mods’ registrations are not removed. Build every definition that the new list refers to before applying it; an invalid replacement leaves the previous list active. 

import io.github.wurtzitane.avogadro.api.*;

public class WaterReplacement {
    public static void replaceWater() {
        var water = AvogadroApi.builder("my_mod:water").name("Water").smiles("[H]O[H]")
                .items("minecraft:water_bucket").fluids("minecraft:water").build();
        var batch = new MoleculeBatch();
        batch.register(water);
        batch.itemTag("my_mod:water_items", false, "minecraft:water_bucket");
        AvogadroApi.owner("my_mod").replace(batch)
            .whenComplete((view, error) -> { if (error != null) error.printStackTrace(); });
    }
}

import io.github.wurtzitane.avogadro.kotlin.Avogadro

fun replaceWater() {
    val water = Avogadro.molecule("my_mod:water") {
        name("Water")
        smiles("[H]O[H]")
        items("minecraft:water_bucket")
        fluids("minecraft:water")
    }
    Avogadro.replace("my_mod") {
        register(water)
        itemTag("my_mod:water_items", false, "minecraft:water_bucket")
    }.whenComplete { view, error -> if (error != null) error.printStackTrace() }
}

mods.avogadro.molecules.batch {
    register('my_pack:water') { smiles('[H]O[H]'); items('minecraft:water_bucket') }
    itemTag('my_pack:water_items', false, ['minecraft:water_bucket'])
}
// This loader's completed contribution replaces its previous script layer.

import io.github.wurtzitane.avogadro.scala.Avogadro

object WaterReplacement {
  def replaceWater(): Unit = {
    val water = Avogadro.molecule("my_mod:water") { builder =>
      builder.name("Water").smiles("[H]O[H]").items("minecraft:water_bucket").fluids("minecraft:water")
    }
    Avogadro.replace("my_mod") { batch =>
      batch.register(water)
      batch.itemTag("my_mod:water_items", false, "minecraft:water_bucket")
    }.whenComplete { (view, error) => if error != null then error.printStackTrace() }
  }
}

import mods.avogadro.Molecules;

val water = Molecules.molecule("my_pack:water")
    .smiles("[H]O[H]")
    .itemSelector("minecraft:water_bucket");
Molecules.transaction("my_pack").replaceAll().register(water)
    .itemTag("my_pack:water_items", false, ["minecraft:water_bucket"])
    .commit();

The Java and CraftTweaker examples replace the definitions and tags owned by the named registration. The GroovyScript loader applies the completed script contribution.

Repeat a connected row of carbon atoms

This places a carbon fragment three times and joins the copies using the connections you specify. Use this pattern for repeated structures. The result has three connected carbon sites; it is an intentionally incomplete chemistry example, with no added hydrogens or inferred reactions. 

var cell = new StructureBuilder().atom("C", 0, 0, 0)
    .cell(new double[][] {{1.42, 0, 0}}).link(0, 0, new int[] {1}).build();
var chain = cell.repeat(new int[] {3}, new boolean[] {false});
var moved = chain.translate(2, 0, 0).rotate(0, 0, 1, 90);

val cell = Avogadro.fragment {
    atom("C", 0.0, 0.0, 0.0)
    cell(arrayOf(doubleArrayOf(1.42, 0.0, 0.0)))
    link(0, 0, intArrayOf(1))
}
val chain = cell.repeat(intArrayOf(3), booleanArrayOf(false))
val moved = chain.translate(2.0, 0.0, 0.0).rotate(0.0, 0.0, 1.0, 90.0)

def cell = molecules.structure {
    atom('C', 0d, 0d, 0d)
    cell([[1.42d, 0d, 0d]] as double[][])
    link(0, 0, [1] as int[])
}
def chain = cell.repeat([3] as int[], [false] as boolean[])
def moved = chain.translate(2d, 0d, 0d).rotate(0d, 0d, 1d, 90d)

val cell = Avogadro.fragment { b =>
  b.atom("C", 0, 0, 0).cell(Array(Array(1.42, 0.0, 0.0))).link(0, 0, Array(1))
}
val chain = cell.repeat(Array(3), Array(false))
val moved = chain.translate(2, 0, 0).rotate(0, 0, 1, 90)

val cell = Molecules.fragment().atom("C", 0.0, 0.0, 0.0)
    .cell([[1.42, 0.0, 0.0]]).link(0, 0, [1], "SINGLE").build();
val chain = cell.repeat([3], [false]);
val moved = chain.translate(2.0, 0.0, 0.0).rotate(0.0, 0.0, 1.0, 90.0);
Molecules.molecule("my_pack:chain").geometry(moved).register();

Transforms return new geometry. Repeat counts and wrap flags have one entry per cell vector. Wrap true connects periodic boundaries without moving coordinates. Cell expansion, affine transforms, append, qualification and cylinder wrapping use the same bounds and topology validation in ZenScript as in Java. See the structures guide for complete operation rules.

Edit a copy and keep the original structure

The example changes a copy while leaving the original fragment available. Atom numbers start at zero. Each operation uses the numbers after the preceding operation, so deletion can change which number refers to an atom. The returned map gives the final number for each original atom, or -1 if it was removed. 

var hydroxyl = new StructureBuilder().atom("O", 0, 0, 0).atom("H", 0.96, 0, 0)
    .bond(0, 1).attachment("oxygen", 0).build();
var result = hydroxyl.edit().moveAtom(1, 0.97, 0, 0).removeAtom(1).build();
int oxygenNow = result.remap(0);
int removedHydrogen = result.remap(1);
var edited = result.fragment();

val hydroxyl = Avogadro.fragment {
    atom("O", 0.0, 0.0, 0.0); atom("H", 0.96, 0.0, 0.0)
    bond(0, 1); attachment("oxygen", 0)
}
val result = Avogadro.edit(hydroxyl) { moveAtom(1, 0.97, 0.0, 0.0); removeAtom(1) }
val oxygenNow = result.remap(0)
val removedHydrogen = result.remap(1)
val edited = result.fragment()

def hydroxyl = molecules.structure {
    atom('O', 0d, 0d, 0d); atom('H', 0.96d, 0d, 0d)
    bond(0, 1); attachment('oxygen', 0)
}
def result = molecules.edit(hydroxyl) { moveAtom(1, 0.97d, 0d, 0d); removeAtom(1) }
def oxygenNow = result.remap(0)
def removedHydrogen = result.remap(1)
def edited = result.fragment()

val hydroxyl = Avogadro.fragment { b =>
  b.atom("O", 0, 0, 0).atom("H", 0.96, 0, 0).bond(0, 1).attachment("oxygen", 0)
}
val result = Avogadro.edit(hydroxyl) { edit =>
  edit.moveAtom(1, 0.97, 0, 0).removeAtom(1)
}
val oxygenNow = result.remap(0)
val removedHydrogen = result.remap(1)
val edited = result.fragment()

val hydroxyl = Molecules.fragment().atom("O", 0.0, 0.0, 0.0)
    .atom("H", 0.96, 0.0, 0.0).bond(0, 1, 1).attachment("oxygen", 0).build();
val result = hydroxyl.edit().moveAtom(1, 0.97, 0.0, 0.0).removeAtoms([1]).build();
val oxygenNow = result.remap(0);
val removedHydrogen = result.remap(1);
val edited = result.geometry;

Bulk removal resolves its whole selection before remapping. Replacing an element clears incompatible atom-specific overrides. Materialize a unit cell or network preview before topology editing. No edit guesses missing bonds, caps or valence repair.

Find the molecule for an item or fluid

After water is registered, these queries find it by molecule ID or by a matching item/fluid stack. Use the running server’s view for server decisions. Use the client view for previews, where the player may have selected a different local model. 

var view = AvogadroApi.registeredView();
var definition = view.get("my_mod:water");
var ids = view.definitions().keySet();
var match = view.find(itemStack); // Actual ItemStack, including metadata and NBT.
var authoritative = AvogadroApi.serverView();

val view = io.github.wurtzitane.avogadro.api.AvogadroApi.registeredView()
val definition = view.get("my_mod:water")
val ids = view.definitions().keys
val match = view.find(itemStack) // Actual ItemStack, including metadata and NBT.
val authoritative = io.github.wurtzitane.avogadro.api.AvogadroApi.serverView()

def view = molecules.view()
def definition = view.get('my_pack:water')
def ids = view.definitions().keySet()
def match = view.find(itemStack) // Actual Minecraft ItemStack.
def authoritative = io.github.wurtzitane.avogadro.api.AvogadroApi.serverView()

val view = io.github.wurtzitane.avogadro.api.AvogadroApi.registeredView()
val definition = view.get("my_mod:water")
val ids = view.definitions().keySet()
val matched = view.find(itemStack) // Actual Minecraft ItemStack.
val authoritative = io.github.wurtzitane.avogadro.api.AvogadroApi.serverView()

val ids = Molecules.ids();
val matchId = Molecules.findItem(<minecraft:water_bucket>);
val fluidId = Molecules.findFluid(<liquid:water>);
val authoritativeIds = Molecules.serverIds();
// Unknown geometry IDs throw; take this snapshot only after registration:
val geometry = Molecules.geometry("my_pack:water");

Java view.get/find return null when absent. ZenScript match methods return an empty string. Query the server view for authoritative decisions; a client’s resource override must never decide a server action. A geometry snapshot remains immutable after the registered definition changes.

Draw water inside a rectangle in your screen

Look up water in the client’s loaded definitions and draw its structure in the rectangle shown below. Call this from your screen’s drawing function on the client render thread. Supply elapsed animation time yourself; the library clips the model to that rectangle and restores the previous graphics state afterward. 

import io.github.wurtzitane.avogadro.api.client.*;

public class WaterPresentation {
    public static void drawWater() {
        var definition = AvogadroClientApi.view().get("my_mod:water");
        if (definition != null) AvogadroClientApi.render(definition.structure(), 12, 40, 240, 180,
            MoleculeRenderOptions.builder().zoom(1.2f).build(), 0.0);
    }
}

import io.github.wurtzitane.avogadro.api.client.*
import io.github.wurtzitane.avogadro.kotlin.AvogadroClient

fun drawWater() {
    val definition = AvogadroClientApi.view().get("my_mod:water")
    if (definition != null) AvogadroClient.render(definition.structure(), 12, 40, 240, 180,
        MoleculeRenderOptions.builder().zoom(1.2f).build(), 0.0)
}

import io.github.wurtzitane.avogadro.api.client.*
def definition = AvogadroClientApi.view().get('my_pack:water')
if (definition != null) AvogadroClientApi.render(definition.structure(), 12, 40, 240, 180,
    MoleculeRenderOptions.builder().zoom(1.2f).build(), 0d)

import io.github.wurtzitane.avogadro.api.client.*
import io.github.wurtzitane.avogadro.scala.AvogadroClient

object WaterPresentation {
  def drawWater(): Unit = {
    val definition = AvogadroClientApi.view().get("my_mod:water")
    if definition != null then AvogadroClient.render(definition.structure(), 12, 40, 240, 180,
      MoleculeRenderOptions.builder().zoom(1.2f).build(), 0.0)
  }
}

// Inside an actual client render event; molecule must exist in the client view:
import mods.avogadro.Client;
Client.renderZoomed("my_pack:water", 12, 40, 240, 180, 1.2, 0.0);

Render options also expose camera orientation, pan, atom/bond scales, palettes, backgrounds and rotation speed. They affect only presentation. Keep client imports out of common/server classes. CPU geometry preparation, GPU lifetime and clipping stay with the existing renderer.

Save a rotating molecule GIF and check the result

This saves a rotating molecule GIF. Submit after the client has loaded the definition, from a client action. Keep the returned job to show progress or request cancellation, and check its final result before opening the output file. 

import io.github.wurtzitane.avogadro.api.client.*;
import io.github.wurtzitane.avogadro.client.export.ExportOptions;

public class WaterPresentation {
    public static void exportWater() throws java.io.IOException {
        var definition = AvogadroClientApi.view().get("my_mod:water");
        if (definition == null) throw new IllegalArgumentException("Water is not loaded");
        var request = MediaExportRequest.molecule(definition)
            .options(ExportOptions.builder(1).size(850, 600).filename("water.gif").build()).build();
        var job = AvogadroClientApi.exports().submit(request);
        job.onComplete(result -> System.out.println(result.state()));
    }
}

import io.github.wurtzitane.avogadro.api.client.*
import io.github.wurtzitane.avogadro.client.export.ExportOptions
import io.github.wurtzitane.avogadro.kotlin.AvogadroClient

fun exportWater() {
    val definition = requireNotNull(AvogadroClientApi.view().get("my_mod:water"))
    val job = AvogadroClient.exportMedia(MediaExportRequest.molecule(definition)) {
        options(ExportOptions.builder(1).size(850, 600).filename("water.gif").build())
    }
    job.onComplete { result -> println(result.state()) }
}

import io.github.wurtzitane.avogadro.api.client.*
import io.github.wurtzitane.avogadro.client.export.ExportOptions
def definition = AvogadroClientApi.view().get('my_pack:water')
if (definition == null) throw new IllegalArgumentException('Water is not loaded')
def request = MediaExportRequest.molecule(definition)
    .options(ExportOptions.builder(1).size(850, 600).filename('water.gif').build()).build()
def job = AvogadroClientApi.exports().submit(request)
job.onComplete { result -> println(result.state()) }

import io.github.wurtzitane.avogadro.api.client.*
import io.github.wurtzitane.avogadro.client.`export`.ExportOptions
import io.github.wurtzitane.avogadro.scala.AvogadroClient

object WaterPresentation {
  def exportWater(): Unit = {
    val definition = AvogadroClientApi.view().get("my_mod:water")
    require(definition != null, "Water is not loaded")
    val job = AvogadroClient.exportMedia(MediaExportRequest.molecule(definition)) { b =>
      b.options(ExportOptions.builder(1).size(850, 600).filename("water.gif").build())
    }
    job.onComplete(result => println(result.state()))
  }
}

import mods.avogadro.Client;
val job = Client.exportSizedGif("my_pack:water", "water.gif", 850, 600);
job.onComplete(function(done) { print(done.state); });
// job.cancel() cancels only this job. Poll capturedFrames, encodedFrames and totalFrames as needed.

Handle both an error while submitting the request and a failure reported by the job later. Only one export runs at a time; a second submission is rejected instead of queued. Completion callbacks run on the client thread after cleanup. The same engine saves galleries, item cards, atoms, and the exact network model you selected. ZenScript exposes these as exportGallery, exportItem, exportAtom and exportNetwork. See the export guide for MP4 encoders and files that record how to rebuild a network.
